messages:
Maya Li: Heads-up: our Next.js starter's eval harness is flaky on CI. The same prompt that passes in the Python LlamaIndex example fails in the JS sample because the streaming output arrives framed differently.
Maya Li: Repro: run `yarn test:e2e` in starter repo, test 'summarize-long-doc' intermittently times out waiting for final chunk.
Owen Park: Which SDK version in the starter?
Maya Li: @Owen it's using @redwood/inference-js v0.9.2 in the starter template. The Python sample uses redwood_inference==0.9.2 as well.
Vikram Das: Can you paste the harness logs? Especially the stream chunk events.
Maya Li: Snippet from harness logs (JS run):
```
[2026-02-28T21:10:01Z] stream: chunk {"delta":"The document provides an overview"}
[2026-02-28T21:10:01Z] stream: chunk {"delta":" of the API and how"}
[2026-02-28T21:10:02Z] stream: chunk {"delta":" to use it."}
[2026-02-28T21:10:02Z] stream: close (no final_summary)
```
Maya Li: Python harness logs show an explicit final chunk: 
```
[2026-02-28T21:10:01Z] stream: chunk {"delta":"The document provides an overview"}
[2026-02-28T21:10:01Z] stream: chunk {"delta":" of the API and how"}
[2026-02-28T21:10:02Z] stream: chunk {"delta":" to use it."}
[2026-02-28T21:10:02Z] stream: chunk {"final":"true","text":"The document provides an overview of the API and how to use it."}
```
Maya Li: The JS SDK sends an implicit close without a final framed message; our eval harness expects a final chunk with 'final' or 'done' field and fails to join tokens deterministically.
Owen Park: Oof. We should have parity here. Historically the JS SDK emitted a 'done' event via the stream controller, but not a framed JSON chunk. The Python SDK includes a final chunk by design.
Vikram Das: Short-term fix in the harness: treat stream close as a final chunk and join deltas. But that's just a bandaid and won't surface the same telemetry shape across SDKs.
Owen Park: Agreed. Better to standardize the streaming framing. Proposal: JS SDK should emit a final chunk object {"final": "true", "text": "..."} before closing the stream so both SDKs produce the same event sequence.
Maya Li: I can patch the starter harness to dodge the flake so CI is green while SDK fix lands. But we should avoid divergence between sample apps and production code paths.
Vikram Das: Long-term: Add a streaming parity test in our SDK acceptance suite that runs both clients against a small mock server and asserts identical chunk sequences (modulo timestamps). Also add a changelog entry for streaming semantics.
Owen Park: I'll open an SDK PR to add the final-chunk emission in JS SDK v0.9.3. Will also add a compatibility flag `streamFrameMode: 'framed' | 'events'` for consumers that rely on the old behavior. Default should be 'framed' for parity.
Maya Li: Patch idea for harness (short-term): update the harness to accept both patterns: either a final framed chunk or a stream close, and canonicalize to the same final text before diffing. I'll send a tiny PR to starter-templates to stop the flaky CI.
QA Bot: Created CI ticket: starter-templates#331 "e2e: fix streaming harness nondeterminism" (P1)
devex-bot: Created SDK issue: platform-sdk#2210 "JS SDK streaming framing parity with Python (emit final chunk)" and assigned to @Owen Park
Owen Park: PR WIP: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/214 (adds final chunk and streamFrameMode flag). Requesting review from eng-ml and devex.
Vikram Das: Also add an eval-harness note in docs/evals.md describing streaming expectations and how to handle partial deltas.
Maya Li: Thanks all. I'll open the harness PR now and link once it's up. This was causing ~3-5% CI flakes across nightly runs so good to stamp down. :rocket:
